title: Supervisor State
body:
The [[Motorola 68000]]'s privileged mode, selected by the S bit in the [[Status Register]].
In supervisor state the processor can execute privileged instructions (including writing
the status register itself) and uses the supervisor stack pointer; in user state it cannot.

Interrupts and exceptions always switch into supervisor state, so an [[ISRs|ISR]] runs
privileged whether or not the interrupted code was.

This is the hardware half of the kernel/user split. [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]] builds the other
half on top: the only legal way for user code to get privileged work done is a
[[System Call]], which is a deliberate exception rather than a jump.
